summary: Opaque 429s from ingress aggregator: requests shown as under quota in console but rejected at edge
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (example: NimbusAI) report unexplained 429 responses during high-volume GraphQL batch ingestion. The Redwood Console shows tenant quota not exhausted and token-level breakdown indicates remaining tokens, but edge returns 429 with no retry-after header in some flows. This appears tied to our new ingress multiplexer (http2 aggregation + sidecar) and the 'annotated-accounting' feature rolled for the dedicated pool last week.

Impact:
- Customer-facing errors for production ingest jobs (binders/QA pipelines) causing partial failure of daily imports.
- Repro rate ~5-10% of batched GraphQL requests during spike windows; when it occurs, many concurrent workers observe repeated 429s and then backoff cascades.

Why this ticket:
Customer requested explanation and immediate mitigation. They are on a dedicated pool and ask for either a hotfix or recommended config to avoid further disruption.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Configure a multiplexing GraphQL uploader to send batches of 10–50 operations over a single HTTP/2 connection with header X-Client-Group: <tenant-id>.
2) Ensure the dedicated pool has 'annotated-accounting' enabled (this was enabled on 2026-03-08).
3) Start 200 parallel worker processes each sending batches at 25 rps per worker for 5 minutes.
4) Observe some requests returning 429 from edge (HTTP/2 stream error) while console token counters remain >0 for the tenant.

Example curl (simplified):
curl -v --http2 -H \"Authorization: Bearer <api_key>\" -H \"X-Client-Group: nimbus-prod\" -d @batch.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/graphql
logs:
Edge proxy logs (truncated):
2026-03-10T09:12:34.112Z E ingress-mux: stream_split id=0x9f2a client=nimbus-prod parts=4 accounting_mode=annotated
2026-03-10T09:12:34.113Z W rate-limiter: tenant=nimbus-prod token_count=42 refill_window=60s decision=REJECT reason=quota-exhausted (per-route accounting)
2026-03-10T09:12:34.114Z I origin: forward request id=0x9f2a-part0 upstream 200
2026-03-10T09:12:34.115Z I origin: forward request id=0x9f2a-part1 upstream 200
2026-03-10T09:12:34.116Z W ingress-mux: counted-as-multiple id=0x9f2a parts_counted=4

Console metrics snapshot (same minute):
tenant=nimbus-prod total_tokens=1000 tokens_used=958 tokens_remaining=42
per-route tokens (showing origin counts): route=/v1/graphql tokens_used=210
per-connection counts (aggregator view): aggregated_tokens=210

Customer-visible response snippet:
HTTP/2 429
:status: 429
content-type: application/json
{"error":"Too many requests"}
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Shah: Customer reported spike of 429s during nightly import. Attached logs and console screenshots. Noted that tokens_remaining shows non-zero.
2026-03-10 Miguel Alvarez (SRE): Assigned. Initial hypothesis: double-counting between edge accounting and origin accounting for split parts. Requested ingress-mux trace IDs and full proxy logs.

2026-03-11 Dana Reed (Platform Eng): Found code path where ingress-mux sets accounting_annotation per sub-request but also increments tenant-level meter on each forward. If annotated-accounting flag is on, we intended to only increment once per original request ID. Patch in PR #1987 changes atomic increment to be guarded by original_request_id dedupe.
investigation_notes:
Reproduced in staging with a dedicated pool mirror and annotated-accounting toggled ON.
- When annotated-accounting=off: no 429s at same load.
- When annotated-accounting=on: intermittent 429s appear and per-part increments are visible in proxy traces.

Token accounting mismatch: edge-level meter increments per internal part; origin-level logs show successful forwards for all parts. The console shows remaining tokens because the aggregator's aggregated counter is updated asynchronously and sometimes lags behind. The rate-limiter (edge) enforces strict token windows and rejects before the aggregated counter reconcile completes.

Root cause (short): ingress-mux iterates parts produced by the batch and calls rate_limiter.claim() for each part without deduping by original_request_id when annotated-accounting enabled. This causes tenant-level token exhaustion during high-concurrency batched uploads.
Related signals: CPU of ingress sidecar spiked 30% during repro; refill-window logs show token_count oscillation (sawtooth) consistent with multiple small claims in same refill period.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied (2026-03-11 03:20 UTC): Turned off annotated-accounting for NimbusAI dedicated pool via control-plane flag rollback (hotfix), which immediately stopped new 429s. Instructed customer to resume jobs; they reported success within 10 minutes.

Root fix merged (2026-03-12): PR https://github.com/redwood/ingress/pull/1987 modifies ingress-mux to attach original_request_id and perform a per-request dedupe before calling rate_limiter.claim(). Also added a unit test for batched requests and an integration test in the rate-limiter suite. PR https://github.com/redwood/rate-limiter/pull/543 adds a short-lived in-memory dedupe cache keyed by original_request_id for the refill window.

Follow-ups:
- INT-2104: Add monitoring alert for 'per-part accounting > aggregated tokens by > 10%' and autopilot to disable annotated-accounting if threshold exceeded.
- Confluence runbook updated: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/ingress-aggregation-accounting-runbook
- Customer billing: Confirm no overage billing for reimbursed rejected requests (CS handling).

Customer communication: Sent incident summary and workaround on 2026-03-11 04:10 UTC. Customer accepted workaround and requested permanent fix timeline; fix deployed to prod 2026-03-12 and verified 2026-03-13.
